### 2026-10-08 – # First Session and Entry 🎉

**3h**

# First Session and Entry 🎉

Yaaay! I finally was able to have some time to work on this project!!

I am so new to hardware and PCB, so I had to follow the Starbie tutorial, but I decided that I will add my own twist into it, by making it into an UFO rather than a star!! Hence, it is called Astrobie 🙂‍↕️

## What I did today
The following are the things I did:
- Downloaded KiCad, and did all the installations that were necessary.
- Followed the guide, in which I completed the schematics...

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/3ae0151c70618f887b8409877885c5b84e759ec7652e9966561dab55c23c94df.png)
- ... and the PCB design.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/6091be46bef418cc737e705cb6b2b922338767344636e52e034eaa3a5a716796.png)

As seen in the image above, I did the required wiring, and I tried to be organized and clean with it at first, but it became messy really quick, with some of the wirings having to take a really big "detour" around the board. I might redesign the board or rearrange the components later on if needed to improve this.

I also managed to run the DRC, but I got WAY more than the expected two errors 😔, so I will look into that next session, which will be tomorrow!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/827339d106d7b996b52b1fe2495678d1e670733afddb8db2bbadb0e119915019.png)

## Tasks for next session
- Fix the errors that the DRC detected
- Reorganize the wiring --> Maybe move around the components to facilitate this
- Keep working on the project!

I am really excited to see hot the final product will turn out!!

Andrés V. (avilldev)
8/10/2026

### 2026-10-09 – # Finishing up the Hardware

**3h**

# Finishing up the Hardware
I kept following the guide, and now I have completed the physical design of the PCB board for my Astrobie!
## What I did
- Realized that the various errors showing up were simply warnings caused by the imported design. Apparently, the two errors that are supposed to appear are not to be taken seriously either, since it will not affect the final, physical result.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/0241690274cd96c2dc64adaf9429ee998a4475a71768f788c4b9ed9a25f25e10.png)
- I still redid the wiring so that it would be more organized.
- Added a GND Pour

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/a0ce2a8f921e2d54a54125501ca37553dfc288ced24e7f43be0a635d7b26896e.png)
- Added image decoration!
- I also took some time to explore the other tools fount in KiCad. One of the things was the Gerber Viewer. I looked into that, and it is the actual blueprint sent to the manufacturer! It does look similar to the interface I edited the PCB in though.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/869cef6add12de161974fc228dc3b59ae6abb7e9fb90890c0c4c6a54a8c37501.png)

## What I have to do next session
- Start working on the Firmware (actual code, yay!)
- Keep following the guide
- I also think that the decorations that I added are too basic, so I might redo that, and be more creative with it.

I also learnt that I can look at a 3D preview, which I find that it's super cool!! This is going to be my project thumbnail now 😋

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/0e0cf027c6247773becbf556b899e9869dc41687fe0bcee9f872eadd1d27f625.png)

### 2026-10-10 – # Started to Code!!

**3h**

# Started to Code!!
I got to the point in the project in which I know more of, to actual program the device! I also realized hhat I haven't been posting reels, so I caught up on it as well.
## What I did this session
- Created and uploaded the reels
- Started the Coding part of the project!
This took me more than it should have 😭. First off, esp32 by Espressif Systems would not fully install in the Arduino IDE. It would be in the process of it, then send out some sort of timeout error each time I tried:

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 164354](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/859f71dc7bd15aa1febec681b627585f56d327859d6ac0c5692338c0894e2b0d.png)
After some restarting the coding steps, as written in the guide, a few time to really make sure that I followed the instructions well, and help from trusty Gemini, it turned out that my Arduino IDE app was not in its latest version 🤦‍♂️. Once I got the latest version installed THEN it worked (yay!), but even then it took several minutes to fully install, but that's fine, as long as I can keep going.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/a1a8eea14b58e1fe632f8efe1f099737d872667d4cbdd97d269759fd27268938.png)
I kept following the instructions, in which I downloaded firmware provided. I drew my pet, which is an alien, using pixel art, and converted it into the required format.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 174234](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/3e4b4bc51d861d23c073d8bd059579bda7df3fec9b223494dc2bf183df600927.png)
I also changed some of the actions to match with my UFO idea: Instead of Nap, Play, Feed, and Pet, it will be called Dock, Fly, Fuel, and Scan.

Before finalizing the code, I wanted to see how the interface would actually look, so I used Wokwi.com for it. I got stuck for a while: even when I pressed the buttons, the menu would not appear. It turns out it was because I wired the buttons incorrectly; instead of diagonally, I put it on the same side. With that fixed, the virtual render seems to be working now, so I really hope that it will also work once I assemble it!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/b771fa390f55d3e7ddeb905c8dfaa813cee5b40cb9cf5a77b98bf94d8f611db9.png)
The one thing I could not test out was the DHT sensor, since the website does not have DHT11 in the library. It does have DHT22 though, so I might see if I can test it out with it.
## What I will do next
- I found out that you can also put images at the back of the PCB somehow, like the example render shows, so I want to figure out how to do that and include it in my project.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/c31ab1f78ae0b110b11123ba91ba443c4f9bf3fd57cd2d7d8d6cde8b4aabf2d8.png)
- I will also finish the customization of the code so it fits the UFO vibe.
- Add a README on GitHub
- Finalize and submit project!

### 2026-10-11 – # Last Session of Week 1!!

**5h**

# Last Session of Week 1!!
I did so much today to finalize the project, but it's done!! 🥳
## What I Did Today
- I kept testing out the code with Wokwi, and I used the DHT22 sensor instead as a temporary replacement. To do this, I simply had to change one value in the code.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/aec92137f60438afd5035819ac303b2595ebd23bd6539d5f59a26e7ce35d8a70.png)
- I did not like the look of the pet on the OLED screen: it was very small and it had this white square background on it.

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 092038](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/b7ba46e5f9f4d2784993dd7a13b50bad5b7e45a462db6b51ee34e25028e82645.png)
I made some changes in the image2cpp website so that the image would be scaled to 64x64, and that the background would be "transparent" (as in, no pixel turned on). I tested it out like that, and finalized on a 64x48 size so that the animation would not be covered by the pet.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/aa5881774413a3b512e3b4d491ab3e1049c37acc0583cc77cf5847cf1d7fe746.png)
- I was looking at the example renders and realized that my pins for the MPU6050 sensor are too close to the button on the right, meaning that the sensor would not fit. Because of this, I had to move the pins in the PCB Editor, rewire the affected wires, and do the ground pour again.

![Untitled drawing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/03be8972ac011909f82d1303505ae7ec952305df272d981602a1b71194e40bec.png)
- In one of my previous journal entries, I wrote that the decorations for my PCB board looked boring. So I did change up the design today, and kind of went crazy with the stars 💫

![Untitled drawing 2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/a3925b611fbd40a5e8bdd6435e18bef65212b907883c635ac7c9e9270a5b745a.png)
- I also previously thought about putting a design on the back. I ended up putting the pet face on the back as a logo. I also added a ground pour on the back as well.

![Untitled drawing 3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/1d47f2bb63bb03a77bae14408cdc68ddd5a0f544f6c49ecf2546a86b7ad66bef.png)
- I added a README.md to my [repository](https://github.com/avilldev/half-life-week1-PCB).
- It took me a while, but I created the BOM. I managed to find the necessary parts all on Alibaba! The PCB will be ordered from JLCPCB.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/f023ee0ddcfabb81f1780e75e47a75bc70a0bb24c18631f4acaf737ea02fd7c4.png)

So that's it!! I am excited to see how it turns out!! I am incredibly grateful for the Starbie guide that Hackclub provided, because without it, I would have no clue as to what to do and I would not have been able to participate in this program.
